quotes.text: But here's the crucial point. Nothing actually disappeared. Your teams weren't deleted, your channels weren't archived, and none of the shared files vanished. They've simply been reorganized under a new framework.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the core misunderstanding behind the redesign: nothing was removed, only reorganized.

quotes.text: Instead of chasing interface changes, shift to what you might call a system's thinking mindset. The aim is to design your team's environment around principles resilient enough to outlast cosmetic updates.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central recommendation for coping with recurring UI changes.

quotes.text: Naming conventions are one of the most boring topics in IT, but they save more time than almost any other practice.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable, practical argument for a habit most teams neglect.

quotes.text: The AI can't pull insights from sloppy data, but an intentional structure, consistent naming, clear usage policies, archives, kept tidy sets you up to take advantage of whatever intelligent layer Microsoft adds on top next year.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links everyday Teams hygiene directly to getting value from Copilot and future AI features.

quotes.text: Your team's never actually disappeared. What disappeared was the shortcut you were used to. The workflow didn't vanish, it just got mapped differently
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise summary that reframes the missing Teams tab as a navigation change.

takeaways: Your teams and channels were not deleted in the new Teams interface; they were folded into a chat-first navigation and are reached through the Teams icon and a few extra clicks.
Pinning priority teams and channels, pinning tabs such as Planner or OneNote, tuning notifications and learning keyboard shortcuts restores a fast daily workflow.
Consistent naming conventions, clear channel usage rules, archiving inactive teams and pinned priorities make your environment resilient to future redesigns and ready for Copilot and Loop.
hook: Opened Microsoft Teams and your Teams tab is gone? This episode is for everyday users and IT admins confused by the new chat-first navigation. You learn where your teams and channels now live and how to build a structure that survives the next redesign.
